correctness.rationale: The complete 90-tetrahedra Björner–Lutz list is available in Lutz 1999 thesis, printed p.17, Theorem 1.5, and the package verify.py reproduces its labelled 90 facet tuples. Inspection of the verifier’s actual Python assertions shows f=(16,106,180,90), all vertex incidence counts with unique degree-8 vertex 16, eight opposite triangles giving an octahedral sphere on {9,10,11,13,14,15}, and precisely missing pairs (9,13),(10,14),(11,15). Those edges all belong to tetrahedra of the deletion. Pure combinatorial argument: an octahedron’s 1-skeleton K_{2,2,2} has clique number3, so every tetrahedron on the six vertices uses at least one opposite pair. As this pair already lies in the unchanged deletion and is absent from the boundary link, any replacement 3-ball intersects deletion beyond the link, impossible by the stated local-replacement definition. Deletion of an open vertex star from the published closed triangulated homology sphere is a homology 3-ball with octahedral boundary and unchanged binary icosahedral pi1 by excision/Mayer–Vietoris and van Kampen. Source topological identification credited, not recomputed. The executable finite verifier itself is not a proof of the external topological identification.
residual_risks: The Poincaré homology-sphere homeomorphism and fundamental group come from published construction, not independently recertified group presentation.
Local deletion fixed throughout; does not establish global 16-vertex minimum.

value.rationale: Vertex removability and minimal local retriangulation are substantive natural obstacles in the 16-vertex combinatorial triangulation of a homology sphere. The distinguished minimal-degree vertex is the most plausible simplification target, so a precise octahedral-diagonal no-go result is an independently useful combinatorial boundary. It does not claim global minimum or a full census.
residual_risks: Does not exclude bistellar sequences changing other simplices or temporary new vertices.

limitations: Single fixed-deletion local vertex elimination only; topology of Poincare sphere taken from primary source.
Unindexed local simplification notes not exhaustively excluded.
